name: RW Aurigae
summary: RW Aurigae is a young variable star whose brightness changes due to stellar rotation and irregular obscuration by circumstellar dust.
why_interesting: RW Aurigae shows both short-term periodic variability and long-lasting irregular dimming events.

facts.label: Distance
facts.compare: The light you see left it about 600 years ago. We do not use another catalogue parallax (15.42 ± 3.69 milliarcseconds, about 210 light-years): its error is 24% and it disagrees with this distance, probably because RW Aurigae is a double star, which spoils the parallax fit.
facts.source: Bailer-Jones et al. (2021), cited in the 2023 RW Aur study

facts.label: Mass
facts.compare: About 34% more massive than the Sun
facts.source: White & Ghez (2001), cited in the 2023 RW Aur study

facts.label: Size
facts.compare: RW Aurigae's radius is about 71% larger than the Sun's.
facts.source: Calculated from published luminosity and effective temperature

facts.label: Temperature
facts.compare: About 13% cooler than the Sun's surface (5,772 K).
facts.source: Pecaut & Mamajek (2013), cited in the 2023 RW Aur study

facts.label: Age
facts.compare: Extremely young compared with our 4.6-billion-year-old Sun
facts.source: Dodin et al. (2020), cited in the 2023 RW Aur study
